newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - slackening ahead of weekend.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - slackening ahead of weekend.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds softened as much as a quarter of a point in subdued, early afternoon trade on Friday, amid speculation prices might slip a bit more from recent highs without breaking the bullish momentum.

"I think the trend over the next couple of weeks still could be bullish but we might have a little setback in here, I just think we've had a pretty good run," a trader said, citing a bit of pressure from profit-takers.
Following the market's drive higher, traders continued to speculate that new issuers, drawn by lower yields, might leap off the shadow calender, though few appeared to be showing their hands.
"Just watch for what surprise deals get brought to market," another trader said.
Next week's calender appeared fairly light, with $1.9 billion of deals expected, down around $1 billion from this week.

Secondary market activity was not particularly active ahead of the summer weekend, though the Standard and Poor's Blue List remained at nearly $1.4 billion. That was roughly $500 million above levels seen early last week.
Actively quoted issues included Jefferson County, Alabama, Sewer Revenues Refunding of 2027, which pay 5-3/8 percent, and were offered at 99-3/4, down one eighth of a point.
And Florida Ports Financing Commission Revenues of 2027, which carry a 5-3/8 percent coupon, were offered at 5.45 percent, NET, up one basis point.

The market discounted a surprising 2.3 percent increase in orders for durable goods, like cars and refrigerators, in June, noting that transportation orders, which make up about a fifth of the report, climbed 7.5 percent. Subtracting that component produced a rise of 0.08 percent, which economists said was consistent with moderate growth.
For the overall report, economists surveyed by Reuters had predicted only a 1.4 percent rise.

A decline in existing home sales furing July largely was predicted by experts. The report showed they fell 2.6 percent to an annualized rate of 4.14 million. Economists had forecast the measure would slip to 4.19 million.

In Chicago futures markets, September municipal futures fell six ticks to 120-27/32, while September Treasury bonds eassed three ticks to 115-7/32. This left the MOB a few ticks lower at plus 180 ticks.
